title: Crosswalk from canonical OKF ONS metadata to statistical, catalogue and provenance vocabularies

assuranceBoundary.statement: Mappings support discovery, comparison and exchange. They do not assert that an upstream product conforms to a vocabulary or that two records are statistically equivalent.

serializationBoundary.statement: SDMX is registered and crosswalked, but the OKF bundle is not serialized as an SDMX message.

sdmxIdentityPolicy.statement: SDMX mappings retain source-native identity, dimension sequence and DSD role rather than flattening components into unordered labels.

mappingKinds.direct: The canonical field and target term have the same intended role at the declared record layer.
mappingKinds.structural: The target model supplies a corresponding class or relation but may require additional transformation.
mappingKinds.broader: The target term is less specific than the canonical field.
mappingKinds.conditional: The mapping is valid only when the record carries the stated evidence or type.
mappingKinds.process: The mapping describes production or provenance rather than catalogue identity.

rules: Never infer equivalence from title or embedding similarity.
Use skos:exactMatch only with evidence of semantic identity; use skos:closeMatch for close but non-equivalent concepts.
Use version predicates only within an evidenced version or succession chain.
Use prov:wasDerivedFrom for derivation and dct:relation for a general relationship when no stronger predicate is evidenced.
A cross-source representation retains both native identifiers and the reconciliation evidence.
Every alternative relationship must expose its material differences or carry not_enough_evidence.

minimumEvidence: authoritative mapping or reviewed semantic-identity evidence

canonicalFields.purpose: Distinguish datasets, series, versions, distributions, data services, catalogue records, concepts and evidence records.

mappings.notes: Select exactly the class supported by the record layer.
Use only for a statistical dataset structure, never for a catalogue record or distribution.
Use only for an actual tabular distribution.

canonicalFields.purpose: Stable source-qualified native identity.

mappings.notes: The source-native identifier remains separately available.

mappings.term: metadata file identifier and resource identifier
mappings.notes: Preserve both identifiers when the GEMINI record supplies them.
Use notation for a code within an explicitly identified classification scheme.

canonicalFields.purpose: Preferred human-readable title without replacing native identity.

mappings.notes: Retain language metadata when supplied.
Use for a concept or code-list item, not automatically for a dataset.
Useful in schema.org dataset JSON-LD export.

canonicalFields.purpose: Source-published aliases, abbreviations and previous titles.

mappings.notes: Preserve alias type and source.
Hidden labels support search but should not be shown as preferred names.
Use for public structured-data export.

canonicalFields.purpose: Source-attributed description of the statistical product.

mappings.notes: Do not replace source description with generated interpretation.
Generated summaries must remain separately labelled.

canonicalFields.purpose: Official-statistics status such as accredited, official or official statistics in development.

mappings.notes: Use the exact current source label and its evidence URL.
Status values can be maintained as a controlled concept scheme.

canonicalFields.purpose: Group releases or versions that belong to one statistical series.

mappings.notes: Do not infer series membership from title similarity.
Map only an evidenced longitudinal or product-series relation.

canonicalFields.purpose: Exact edition and version identity, succession and notes.

mappings.notes: Preserve native edition and version components as well as display form.
A changed version is not automatically a correction.
Use when the profile representation calls for ADMS version notes.

canonicalFields.purpose: Organisation responsible for making the asset available.

mappings.notes: Distinguish publisher from creator, owner and statistical producer.
Use explicit associations to distinguish organisational roles.
Use in schema.org export.

canonicalFields.purpose: Reference period and coverage, distinct from release, issue and modification dates.

mappings.notes: Encode bounded dates and intervals using ISO 8601 forms.
Keep publication dates in separate fields.

canonicalFields.purpose: Expected publication or observation frequency.

mappings.notes: Use an identified controlled value where available.
Preserve the source code and code-list identity.

canonicalFields.purpose: Statistical universe or population represented by the product.

mappings.notes: Preserve inclusion, exclusion and reference-time evidence.
Use as an information-model mapping, not a replacement identifier.

canonicalFields.purpose: Statistical subject or characteristic being measured.

mappings.notes: Preserve concept-scheme membership and mapping strength.
Retain agency, identifier and version.
May participate in a represented-variable mapping.

canonicalFields.purpose: Measured quantity, indicator or statistic.

mappings.notes: Keep measure identity distinct from unit.
Preserve source DSD role and concept identity.
Useful for public dataset structured data.

canonicalFields.purpose: Unit, scale, denominator or basis needed to interpret the measure.

mappings.notes: Map a unit attribute when the source structure identifies it.
Keep agency, identifier and version with both the source code and readable label.

canonicalFields.purpose: Selection dimensions belonging to an exact dataset version.

mappings.notes: Associate dimensions with the exact data-structure definition.
Dimension order and role are significant where the source specifies them.
Use when concept and value domain evidence is available.

canonicalFields.purpose: Allowed option vocabularies with codes, labels, hierarchy and version.

mappings.notes: Reference the code list rather than duplicating it per observation.
Preserve hierarchy and source-native notation.
Retain agency, identifier and version.

canonicalFields.purpose: Valid and invalid combinations for a dataset-version selection plan.

mappings.notes: Use source constraints to prune impossible combinations.
Use only for constraints actually expressed by a tabular distribution.

canonicalFields.purpose: Geography level, code family, reference vintage, CRS, extent and boundary variant.

mappings.term: geographic bounding box, reference system and spatial-resolution metadata
mappings.notes: Preserve profile version and validation evidence.
Map through a public implementation profile.
Use a bounded extent or named geography; full geometry remains external.

canonicalFields.purpose: Producer-published methods, collection, sampling, processing and adjustment evidence.

mappings.notes: Keep limitations and planned changes with the method.
Map only what the source publishes.
Useful for a concise public structured-data summary.

canonicalFields.purpose: Source-published and independently measured quality evidence with method and provenance.

mappings.notes: Identify whether the evidence is producer-supplied or bundle-evaluated.
Preserve source wording and URL.

mappings.term: ISO 19157 quality element, measure, evaluation and result
mappings.notes: Use only for geographic-quality evidence.

canonicalFields.purpose: Uncertainty, error, bias, confidence, representativeness and known limitations.

mappings.notes: Prominence is part of the user-facing contract.
Keep evidence attributed to the product and version.
Use a typed annotation with evidence provenance.

canonicalFields.purpose: Revision or correction type, reason, timing and affected versions.

mappings.notes: Use the producer's explicit classification.
Version relations do not by themselves distinguish revision from correction.
Use only where a revision relation is evidenced.

canonicalFields.purpose: Recognised classifications, definitions, harmonised standards and deviations.

mappings.term: ONS classification scheme, version and code
mappings.notes: Preserve the scheme edition.

mappings.term: GSS harmonised standard and implementation evidence
mappings.notes: Similar wording is not enough to claim harmonisation.
Use mappings with an explicit strength and evidence.

canonicalFields.purpose: Evidence about how the statistical product is specified, acquired, processed, analysed and disseminated.

mappings.notes: Undocumented phases remain not-evidenced.
Distinguish statistical production from bundle transformation.
Apply to products using administrative data.

canonicalFields.purpose: Source URL, native identifier, retrieval, content digest and transformation lineage.

mappings.term: prov:Entity | prov:Activity | prov:Agent | prov:wasDerivedFrom | prov:hadPrimarySource | prov:generatedAtTime
mappings.notes: Never publish a local cache path.
Use for a human-readable provenance statement.

canonicalFields.purpose: Typed alternatives, succession, derivation, different-grain and cross-source representations.

mappings.notes: Use for semantic concept relationships with explicit strength.
Use a qualified relation when role or evidence needs representation.
Use for provenance and representation relations, not topical similarity.

canonicalFields.purpose: Downloads, APIs and services through which the data may be accessed.

mappings.notes: Keep the service distinct from the dataset and distribution.
Do not synthesize an unsupported upstream API contract.
Use for public structured-data discovery.

canonicalFields.purpose: Licence, rights, security classification, authentication and access restrictions.

mappings.notes: Use persistent licence identifiers where supplied.

mappings.term: use limitation, use constraints and access constraints
mappings.notes: Keep distinct constraints distinct.

canonicalFields.purpose: Requirement-level source evidence and separate bundle-profile validation.

mappings.notes: A standards-evidence claim is not a quality certification.
Use only for the bundle profile or an explicit source-published conformance assertion.
Retain the evidence source and evaluation activity.
